title: Rot Spread Time
statement:
Compute how many minutes it takes for every fresh item in a grid to rot, or report that some never will.

Contract
- `grid` is a rectangular array holding `0` (empty), `1` (fresh) or `2` (rotten); it may have no rows.
- Each minute, every fresh cell that shares an edge (up, down, left or right) with a rotten cell becomes rotten. All cells change at the same moment, so spreading starts from every rotten cell at once.
- Return the number of minutes until no fresh cell remains. Return 0 if there was no fresh cell to begin with.
- Return -1 if some fresh cell can never rot. Do not modify `grid`.

Examples
- `minutesToRot(new int[][]{{0,1,1,1},{1,2,1,0}})` returns `3`.
- `minutesToRot(new int[][]{{2,0,1}})` returns `-1`: the empty cell blocks the spread.
- `minutesToRot(new int[][]{{0,2},{0,0}})` returns `0`.
hints: Rot spreads outward in rounds, like ripples, and every rotten cell starts spreading in the very first round.
Put all initially rotten cells in a queue and process it one round at a time, turning fresh neighbours rotten and queuing them. Count the fresh cells so you know when you are done.

Count a minute only for rounds that rot something, and compare the remaining fresh count with zero at the end to decide between the answer and -1. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the queue, where n is the number of cells.
inputSyntax: Input: the grid rows as nested lists using 0 (empty), 1 (fresh) and 2 (rotten), for example: [[0, 1, 1, 1], [1, 2, 1, 0]]
